results.name: Axum
results.workers: Tokio multi-threaded runtime, one worker per available CPU (2)
results.database_layer: SQLx 0.9 (Axum has no ORM; its examples use SQLx)

results.name: Actix Web
results.workers: Default: one worker per available CPU (2)

results.name: Loco
results.workers: Tokio multi-threaded runtime, one worker per available CPU (2)
results.logging: Loco logger at warn level (no per-request logs)

results.name: Rullst
results.workers: Tokio multi-threaded runtime, one worker per available CPU (2)
results.logging: Rullst's access log (one stdout line per request; Server has no switch to turn it off)

results.name: Rullst
results.workers: Tokio multi-threaded runtime, one worker per available CPU (2)

results.name: Topcoat
results.workers: Tokio multi-threaded runtime, one worker per available CPU (2)
results.logging: none (Topcoat logs nothing per request by default)
results.maturity_note: early 0.x framework, measured with its documented defaults

results.name: ASP.NET Core
results.workers: .NET thread pool sized by the runtime for 2 vCPUs; Server GC (the ASP.NET Core default)
results.database_layer: Entity Framework Core 10.0 with the Npgsql provider, pool of 16 connections
results.logging: none per request (Microsoft.AspNetCore and EF Core command logs at Warning); start-up log at Information

results.name: Django
results.database_layer: Django ORM with psycopg 3.3 (C extension); persistent connections (CONN_MAX_AGE), one per thread, 16 in total
results.logging: none (Gunicorn's access log is off; Django logs only warnings and errors)

results.name: Laravel
results.server: Nginx with PHP-FPM, as in Laravel's deployment documentation
results.workers: Nginx: BENCH_WORKERS (2) workers; PHP-FPM: the default pool (pm = dynamic, at most 5 processes)
results.database_layer: Eloquent (pdo_pgsql); one connection per PHP-FPM process, opened for each request (at most 5)
results.logging: none (Nginx and PHP-FPM access logs off; Laravel logs warnings and errors to stderr)

results.name: NestJS
results.runtime: Node.js 26.13.1 LTS, NODE_ENV=production, compiled with nest build (tsc)
results.database_layer: TypeORM 1.1 via @nestjs/typeorm with pg, 8 connections per process (16 in total)
results.logging: none per request (Nest has no request logger); start-up log per process

results.name: Phoenix
results.workers: One BEAM node; one scheduler online per CPU the container may use (2)
results.database_layer: Ecto 3.14 with Postgrex, pool of DB_POOL_SIZE (16) connections

results.name: Ruby on Rails
results.server: Puma 8.1 behind Thruster 0.1, as in the Dockerfile rails new generates
results.workers: Puma cluster mode: WEB_CONCURRENCY = BENCH_WORKERS (2) workers x 3 threads (the generated RAILS_MAX_THREADS default)
results.database_layer: Active Record (pg 1.7), up to 8 connections per worker (16 in total)
results.logging: Rails at warn (no request lines); Thruster's request log off

results.name: Spring Boot
results.runtime: Java 25 (Eclipse Temurin 25.0.5 JRE), layered executable jar, no JVM flags
results.server: Spring MVC on embedded Tomcat 11 (the starter's default)
results.workers: Tomcat's default request thread pool (up to 200 threads); JVM ergonomics for 2 vCPUs and 2 GiB
results.database_layer: Spring Data JPA (Hibernate 7.4), HikariCP pool of 16 connections
results.logging: none per request (Tomcat's access log is off by default); start-up log at INFO

results.name: FastAPI
results.workers: BENCH_WORKERS Uvicorn worker processes (2), one event loop each
results.database_layer: SQLModel 0.0.50 on SQLAlchemy 2.1 with psycopg 3 (sync sessions, as in the FastAPI SQL tutorial), DB_POOL_SIZE / BENCH_WORKERS connections per process
results.problem: /db-single is not measured in this run: under load every request timed out because of a defect in this implementation (the session dependency's cleanup waited for a thread-pool slot held by requests waiting for a database connection), so the number says nothing about FastAPI. Fixed in Rullst/Benchmarks#8; the next run (Rullst 13.0.0-alpha.6) measures it again.

results.name: Fastify
results.database_layer: @fastify/postgres 6.1 (node-postgres 8.23 pool), DB_POOL_SIZE / BENCH_WORKERS connections per process
results.logging: none (Fastify's logger is off by default)

results.name: Gin
results.workers: One process; the Go scheduler runs goroutines on GOMAXPROCS threads, which defaults to the 2 available CPUs
results.database_layer: GORM 1.31 with gorm.io/driver/postgres 1.6 (pgx 5), one database/sql pool of DB_POOL_SIZE connections
results.logging: none (gin.New() without the Logger middleware, GORM logger silent)

metrics.json_rps: Tier 1 /json, 125 connections: successful responses per second (median of rounds)
metrics.db_single_rps: Tier 1 /db-single, 125 connections: successful responses per second
metrics.avg_latency_ms: Tier 1 /json, 125 connections: mean latency in milliseconds
metrics.peak_ram_mib: Tier 3, 200 connections on /json: peak RAM of the server container in MiB
metrics.vs_axum: median of per-round ratios to Axum measured on the same runner (1.0 = Axum)
metrics.load_generator_bound_rounds: rounds in which the load generator's CPUs were at least 90% busy

auto_update: updated automatically when a new rullst version is published on crates.io
note: This measurement found a throughput problem in the production stack that `cargo rullst new` generates: Rullst as generated reached 0.31× Axum's requests/s on /json, while the minimal configuration reached 1.00×. A fix is planned for Rullst 13.0.0-alpha.6. These results update automatically when a new Rullst version is published.
note_pt_br: Esta medição encontrou um problema de vazão na pilha de produção que o `cargo rullst new` gera: o Rullst como gerado chegou a 0,31× as requisições/s do Axum em /json, enquanto a configuração mínima chegou a 1,00×. Uma correção está planejada para o Rullst 13.0.0-alpha.6. Estes resultados se atualizam automaticamente quando uma nova versão do Rullst é publicada.
